title: An hour of prayer (II.1)
hook: he recommends a daily hour of mental prayer, early if possible
tomorrow: how do you take a prayer with you when you leave?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the first meditations: made out of nothing, to show God's goodness, with every gift a tool for it. The line was why made.

The weekly screen-time report lands like a verdict: hours, every day, on one small glass rectangle. So when Francis de Sales asks for one hour a day of prayer, the honest reaction is: who has that? Part two of his book turns to prayer, and it opens on exactly that number. Then, in the same breath, he makes room for the life you actually have.
screen: `THE SCREEN-TIME REPORT.` → `AN HOUR? WHO HAS THAT?` → `ROOM FOR THE LIFE YOU HAVE.`

segments.voice: The question is simple: when should a person pray? De Sales recommends mental prayer, the prayer of the heart, above all on the life and passion of Jesus. Children learn to speak by listening to their mothers, he says; we learn Christ's ways by keeping company with him. An hour a day, and no more without your guide's advice. Early in the morning if you can, when the mind is fresh after the night. If the morning gets swallowed, make it up later, though not right after a meal, when you'd only be drowsy. And if the whole day slips, repair it with short prayers and begin again. Now a neighbor who also prizes the dawn. In the Qur'an, God tells the Prophet to keep up the prayer from the sun's decline into the dark of night, and the recitation at dawn, which the verse says is witnessed. Here's the shared thing to tell a friend: two traditions, two languages, both pointing at first light. And one honest difference: salah, the Muslim ritual prayer, has set words and movements at set times; de Sales's hour is mostly silent prayer of the heart, and its time can move.
screen: `WHEN SHOULD A PERSON PRAY?` · `AN HOUR, EARLY IF YOU CAN.` · `IF THE MORNING'S LOST, MAKE IT UP.` · `THE QUR'AN: THE DAWN IS WITNESSED.` · then, large: `AN HOUR, IF YOU CAN.`

segments.voice: Let these two minutes be the first small slice of that hour. Say the Our Father out loud, slowly, one phrase per breath, and when a phrase holds you, stop there and stay. If you don't pray, say one line you love, aloud, the same way.
An hour of prayer. Francis de Sales's counsel: a daily hour of mental prayer, early if possible, made up later if the morning is lost.
Pocket this one: an hour, if you can, and the if is part of the counsel. That's day 1497.

notes: Introduction II.1 paraphrased: mental prayer, especially on the life and passion of our Lord; children learn to speak by listening to their mothers; an hour every day before dinner, if possible early in the morning when the mind is less distracted and fresher after the night's rest; no more than an hour unless your spiritual father directs; if the morning is lost, repair it later, but not right after a meal; vocal prayers (Our Father, Hail Mary, Creed) kept, and the heart may be drawn into mental prayer.
